evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.text: The entry analyzes early 出 as 止 above 凵, with some oracle-bone examples using 囗. It interprets 止 as a foot and 凵/囗 as a cave or dwelling, yielding ‘step out’. It cites oracle-bone examples 合集5063 王出, 合集33006 出日, and 合集7205 勿出兵, and bronze-inscription examples involving going out, paying cloth, and issuing or transmitting commands. These examples attest varied contexts but do not establish their relative chronology.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「出」

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, 漢字字形演變資料庫
evidence.text: The database describes the upper part of oracle-bone and bronze forms as 止, a foot, and the lower part as a cave-like form. It lists oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, and small-seal categories, but the accessible text does not date individual oracle-bone specimens or give a fully dated sequence of graphic changes.
evidence.title: 漢字「出」：字形演變

evidence.source: 裘錫圭, Fudan University Center for the Study and Preservation of Excavated Texts
evidence.field: 甲骨文字形與《說文》解釋
evidence.text: Qiu analyzes the oracle-bone graph as a foot moving outward from a hollow or dwelling. He argues that the small-seal form available to Xu Shen obscured the earlier shape and that the plant-growth explanation in Shuowen should not be treated as confirmation of the graph’s original form. This is a scholar’s interpretation of the graphic evidence.
evidence.title: 裘錫圭：殷墟甲骨文在文字學上的重要性

evidence.text: This secondary collation describes oracle-bone and bronze 出 as 止 plus 凵, with an occasional 囗 variant. It proposes that the parts joined graphically and that later clerical and regular forms made 止 resemble 屮, helping explain the Shuowen plant reading. It indexes oracle-bone, bronze, Warring States, seal, and Qin-slip examples, but supplies no exact first-use date; the corruption sequence is the page’s analysis, not an independently verified glyph-by-glyph chronology.
evidence.title: 汉字「出」字形演变字源

evidence.source: 《說文解字》 text reproduced in 漢語多功能字庫
evidence.text: The entry reproduces Xu Shen’s explanation: “進也。象艸木益滋，上出達也” (“advance; images plants growing luxuriantly and emerging upward”). This is an early lexicographic account of the graph, distinct from modern interpretations based on oracle-bone forms.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「出」

evidence.text: The authors’ table gives 出 ‘go or come out’ as Middle Chinese tsyhwit and Old Chinese *t-kʰut; it separately lists ‘bring or take out’ as tsyhwijH and *t-kʰut-s. The table identifies these as word readings and reconstructions, not a phonetic component inside the graph. It does not establish the chronology of the senses.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1 (20 September 2014)

evidence.text: The inspected entry gives modern Mandarin chū and Cantonese ceot1, and reproduces Shuowen and later dictionary material. It lists senses including going out, emerging, sending out, producing, and standing, with literary citations; the page does not establish a chronological derivation among those senses. Its cited Guangyun readings distinguish entering- and departing-tone categories.
evidence.title: 出 chū - 漢典

evidence.source: Wikimedia Commons file description reproduced on Wiktionary

evidence.text: The description identifies 出-oracle.svg as a digital vector rendering of an oracle-script form, cites the Sears ChineseEtymology reference J15041 and paleographic databases as sources, and marks the file public domain. It is a modern redraw, not a photograph of an ancient artifact. The linked original-file URL was obtained, but fetching the SVG returned a cache miss; its pixels were not inspected.

gaps: The inspected sources identify oracle-bone examples, including 合集5063 王出, but do not provide a securely dated earliest token or a precise date for that inscription. The earliest attested graph and an exact first-use date remain unestablished here.

The early foot-plus-enclosure analysis is supported by paleographic database descriptions. The proposed sequence in which the parts joined and 止 later became visually confused with 屮 is stated by a secondary collation; a primary glyph-by-glyph demonstration of that transition was not inspected.

The oracle-bone examples include motion, sunrise, and sending troops; bronze examples include going out, paying cloth, and issuing or transmitting commands. These examples do not establish a complete chronological sequence or the semantic links to later senses such as ‘produce’ and ‘stand’.

No phonetic component is proposed by the inspected paleographic analyses. The readings and Old Chinese reconstructions concern the spoken word(s) written 出, not an internal sound component. The dossier’s Zhengzhang reconstructions differ from Baxter–Sagart’s; their rationale and variant scope were not independently checked against a primary Zhengzhang source.

No independent evidence was found here for the proposed Tibeto-Burman cognacy, or for a historical whole-graph borrowing involving 出. The modern and later dictionary glosses do not by themselves establish either claim.

The Zdic page lists several meanings and citations, but this research did not verify the dates of all cited texts or establish chronology from that gloss list. The specific histories of ‘send out’, ‘produce’, ‘stand’, and the ‘scene/section’ use associated with 齣 remain unresolved.

No glyph image was visually inspected. The one proposed file is described by its source page as a modern vector redraw, not an ancient artifact photograph. Its direct file fetch failed with a cache miss.
